newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Feb INPC inflation fell to 0.45 pct - IBGE.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Feb INPC inflation fell to 0.45 pct - IBGE.

text.p: Brazilian inflation in February as measured by the National Consumer Prices Index (INPC) was 0.45 percent, down from 0.81 percent in January, the government's National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.
The INPC is based on the spending of families earning up to eight minimum salaries.

The Wider Consumer Price Index (IPCA), which measures the spending of families earning up to 40 salaries, registered inflation of 0.50 percent in February against 1.19 percent the previous month, the IBGE added in a statement.
February's results means the cumulative INPC index in the first two months of this year is now 1.26 percent and in the case of the IPCA, 1.69 percent.
Housing was the principal factor behind February's 0.45 percent variation in the INPC index, with rent and service charges seeing inflation of 1.17 percent.
Clothing and personal expenses however registered deflation of 0.85 percent and 0.05 percent respectively, the IBGE said.
The same pattern was repeated in the IPCA index, it added. ((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
